page: Amazon Web Services c8in.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The instance is built on x86_64 architecture utilizing an Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Its configuration supplies 2 vCPUs derived from 1 dedicated physical core with 2 threads per core. System memory is provisioned at 4.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Storage and connectivity rely fully on network infrastructure, as the c8in.large instance includes no local storage volumes. Disk I/O must be fulfilled via network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes. Network capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps with integrated EBS and network optimizations. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and operates without GPU hardware acceleration.

Given its 3.9 GHz processor speed and dedicated core allocation, the server is architected for compute-bound operations that do not require substantial memory capacity. Tradeoffs include memory density constraints and dependence on remote storage for all persistence. The instance is suited for tasks such as batch data processing, distributed worker nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and stateless web serving.
